title: Rigveda 7.51: To Adityas
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.51: To Adityas: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.51 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Adityas. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 525v-526r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.51.1 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 4, varga 18); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 525v
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ā̱di̱tyānā̱m ava̍sā̱ nūta̍nena sakṣī̱mahi̱ śarma̍ṇā̱ śaṁta̍mena | a̱nā̱gā̱stve a̍diti̱tve tu̱rāsa̍ i̱maṁ ya̱jñaṁ da̍dhatu̱ śroṣa̍māṇāḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>THROUGH the Âdityas' most auspicious shelter, through their most recent succour may we conquer. May they, the Mighty, giving ear, establish this sacrifice, to make us free and sinless.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 525v (numbered 46v by the scribe) (OPenn image 526, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.50.1 ‹-mitrāvaruṇā iha rakṣatam kulāyayat›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 526r (numbered 47r by the scribe), begins in RV 7.51.2 ‹bhuvanasya gopāḥ pibantu somam›. Verse 7.51.1 ends on this page.
translation.edition_text: <sup>1</sup>ādityānām | avasā | nūtanena | sakṣīmahi | śarmaṇā | śam-tamena | anāgāḥ-tve | aditi-tve | turāsaḥ | imam | yajñam | dadhatu | śroṣamāṇāḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 7.51.2-3 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 4, varga 18); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 526r
translation.original_text:
2ā̱di̱tyāso̱ adi̍tir mādayantām mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā varu̍ṇo̱ raji̍ṣṭhāḥ | a̱smāka̍ṁ santu̱ bhuva̍nasya go̱pāḥ piba̍ntu̱ soma̱m ava̍se no a̱dya ||
3ā̱di̱tyā viśve̍ ma̱ruta̍ś ca̱ viśve̍ de̱vāś ca̱ viśva̍ ṛ̱bhava̍ś ca̱ viśve̍ | indro̍ a̱gnir a̱śvinā̍ tuṣṭuvā̱nā yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
2Let Aditi rejoice and the Âdityas, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, most righteous. May they, the Guardians of the world, protect us, and, to show favour, drink this day our Soma.
3All Universal Deities, the Maruts, all the Âdityas, yea, and all the R̥ibhus, Indra, and Agni, and the Aṣvins, lauded. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 526r (numbered 47r by the scribe) (OPenn image 526, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.51.2 ‹bhuvanasya gopāḥ pibantu somam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 526v (numbered 47v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.53.2 ‹ṛtasya ā naḥ dyāvāpṛthivī›. Verses 7.51.2-3 end on this page; 7.51.2 begins on fol. 525v (numbered 46v by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
2ādityāsaḥ | aditiḥ | mādayantām | mitraḥ | aryamā | varuṇaḥ | rajiṣṭhāḥ | asmākam | santu | bhuvanasya | gopāḥ | pibantu | somam | avase | naḥ | adya
3ādityāḥ | viśve | marutaḥ | ca | viśve | devāḥ | ca | viśve | ṛbhavaḥ | ca | viśve | indraḥ | agniḥ | aśvinā | tustuvānāḥ | yūyam | pāta | svasti-bhiḥ | sadā | naḥ
